lessons_used: Evidence is still thin for all specific kinds of change because each kind has only been tested once.
Predictions were consistently too high across all tests compared to measured and noise-corrected results.

candidates.title: Spotlight layout redesign for choose path screen
candidates.change: Redesign the choose path screen using a spotlight layout that focuses on one onboarding path at a time with clear visual highlights.
candidates.why: Path selection takes a high mean duration of 514s and converting 76.8%; a spotlight layout reduces cognitive load.

guard.reason: Redesigning the choose path screen layout inside onboarding is allowed and retains path options.

candidates.score_note: Addresses high duration on choose_path (76.8% conv), but layout changes previously yielded weak results (+0.6%) and requires a full redesign.

candidates.title: Interactive personality companion pitch on app intro
candidates.change: Update the story screen copy to highlight how virtual pets interact with your daily desktop environment.
candidates.why: Clarifies desktop app capabilities upfront before users commit to choosing an onboarding path.

story.headline: Meet Your Perfect Desktop Companion
story.body: Discover how a virtual pet can keep you company, boost focus, and brighten your daily work routine right on your screen.

guard.reason: Story screen copy update introduces the pet without mentioning pricing or breaking rules.

candidates.score_note: Low cost text update for choose_path step; unsupported by user tickets but simple to deploy.

candidates.title: Split layout redesign with account benefits on sign in
candidates.change: Redesign the sign-in screen into a split layout showing desktop pet cloud sync benefits beside sign-in options.
candidates.why: Sign-in conversion is 72.9% and support received 8 emails regarding missing or reset pets when re-authenticating.

guard.reason: Split layout redesign for sign-in is allowed within onboarding.

candidates.score_note: Strong evidence combining 72.9% conversion drop with 8 support tickets, but requires layout redesign.

candidates.title: Existing pet sync restore hint on sign in screen
candidates.change: Add an explicit hint on sign-in clarifying that signing in restores existing pets and saved progress.
candidates.why: Addresses 8 support tickets from users confused about pet state resets when logging back in.

sign_in.hint: Sign in with your registered account to automatically restore your existing desktop pets and settings.

guard.reason: Adding a sign-in hint explaining restore functionality is permitted.

candidates.score_note: Directly targets 8 support tickets and 72.9% conversion drop via low-cost hint text; hints showed positive historical lift.

candidates.title: Interactive pet preview screen during adoption
candidates.change: Insert a dedicated animation preview screen after picking a friend to showcase pet actions before certificate generation.
candidates.why: Adoption has the lowest conversion rate at 60.9%; letting users preview pet behaviors increases emotional investment.

pick_friend.hint: Preview your pet's desktop behaviors before finalizing adoption.

guard.reason: _order names screens that are neither onboarding screens nor defined here: ['new_pet_preview']

candidates.title: Move sign in after pet adoption certificate
candidates.change: Reorder the flow so users create and adopt their pet before signing in to save their progress.
candidates.why: Adoption is the biggest drop-off point (60.9%); delaying account creation until after pet creation builds intent.

guard.reason: Reordering sign-in after adoption certificate is explicitly allowed.

candidates.score_note: Targets largest drop-off step (adoption at 60.9%), but re-ordering flows carries high risk (new_flow yielded -1.0% previously).

candidates.title: Stage layout display for adoption certificate screen
candidates.change: Change the adoption certificate screen to a stage layout showcasing the completed pet certificate prominently.
candidates.why: Improves visual celebration during adoption stage where users spend median 89s / mean 1017s.

guard.reason: Stage layout redesign for adoption certificate retains the screen's core job.

candidates.score_note: Targets highest drop-off step (60.9% adoption), but evidence lacks support tickets and layout changes show minimal lift.

candidates.title: Desk environment sound player on waiting screen
candidates.change: Add an ambient sound player component on the waiting screen so users can listen to cozy desk audio while generation runs.
candidates.why: The waiting step has a long mean time of 2336s; audio relaxation keeps users engaged.

guard.reason: Adding an ambient sound player component to the waiting screen is allowed.

candidates.score_note: Directly supported by prior wait_info test (+2.1%), though home already has high base conversion (81.3%).

candidates.title: Desktop ready notification toggle on waiting screen
candidates.change: Enable a system desktop notification alert option on the waiting screen when pet rendering completes.
candidates.why: Mean waiting time is 2336s; users minimize the window and benefit from an automatic tray alert when done.

waiting.body: Your pet is being prepared! We will notify your desktop the moment it is ready.

guard.reason: Enabling desktop ready notifications on the waiting screen is allowed.

candidates.score_note: Addresses long wait times, but notification changes previously resulted in negative lift (-1.8%).

candidates.title: Desktop control checklist flow on home welcome screen
candidates.change: Transform the home intro screen into an interactive checklist teaching how to hide, drag, and talk to the pet.
candidates.why: 3 support tickets specifically reported post-onboarding confusion around controlling and hiding pets on desktop.

components.text: Try moving, hiding, and right-clicking your pet on desktop

guard.reason: Updating home_intro layout and adding interactive checklist components within onboarding is allowed.

candidates.score_note: Supported by 3 support tickets regarding desktop controls, though flow changes require high effort and carry moderate uncertainty.

lessons_next: Evidence is still thin for almost all specific kinds of change, as only 'home, wait_info' has been tested more than once.
For 'home, wait_info', one test won while one showed no clear effect, so a definitive pattern is not yet established.
Helpful changes were observed in tests for 'choose_path, hint', 'finish, new_screen', and 'home, wait_info' because those tests won.
No effect was seen for tests in 'home, new_flow', 'adoption, notification', 'sign_in, incentive', 'choose_path, layout', and 'adoption, layout'.
Predictions were generally too high for most tests, though they underpredicted gains on certain winning tests like 'finish, new_screen' and 'home, wait_info'.
